answer: Reaching the basalt of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts split across independent auditors. Each submission hangs on the sable of a task receipt, and the orchard is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a concise reports, one example per claim register, it stays short.
